item_name: Pneumonia (Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days — Infections)

lookback_source.quote: Diagnosis status: Active or Inactive (Step 2) is a 7-day look-back period (except for Item I2300 UTI, which does not use the active 7-day look-back period).

lookback_notes: Two look-back periods apply to this section. The assessor's observation window for determining whether the diagnosis is ACTIVE is 7 days (p. I-8); counted per the general convention as ARD + 6 previous calendar days (rai-manual-v1.20.1, p. 2-17: "ARD + 6 previous calendar days"). A separate 60-day window applies to Step 1, diagnosis identification: the disease must have a physician-documented diagnosis in the last 60 days (p. I-8, p. I-9). The 30-day exception stated for the section applies only to Item I2300 UTI, not to I2000.

coding_levels.label: I2000 Pneumonia checked (active diagnosis present)
coding_levels.definition: Check the I2000 Pneumonia box when pneumonia is a physician-documented diagnosis in the last 60 days that has a direct relationship to the resident's current functional status, cognitive status, mood or behavior status, medical treatments, nursing monitoring, or risk of death during the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Code diseases that have a documented diagnosis in the last 60 days and have a direct relationship to the resident’s current functional status, cognitive status, mood or behavior status, medical treatments, nursing monitoring, or risk of death during the 7-day look-back period

coding_levels.label: I2000 Pneumonia not checked (inactive/not present)
coding_levels.definition: Leave the box blank when the pneumonia diagnosis is not active — e.g., the resident has recovered completely, with no residual effects and no continued treatment during the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Coding: Pneumonia item (I2000), would not be checked.

federal_coding_rules.rule: I2000 Pneumonia is one of the checkbox diagnoses in the Infections category of Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days; check all that apply.

source.quote: I2000. Pneumonia

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code the disease only if it has a documented diagnosis in the last 60 days AND has a direct relationship to the resident's current functional status, cognitive status, mood or behavior status, medical treatments, nursing monitoring, or risk of death during the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Code diseases that have a documented diagnosis in the last 60 days and have a direct relationship to the resident’s current functional status, cognitive status, mood or behavior status, medical treatments, nursing monitoring, or risk of death during the 7-day look-back period

federal_coding_rules.rule: The diagnosis must be physician-documented (or documented by a nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) in the last 60 days.

source.quote: The disease conditions in this section require a physician-documented diagnosis (or by a nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) in the last 60 days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not check the item for conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident's current status, or do not drive the resident's plan of care during the 7-day look-back period; these are inactive diagnoses.

source.quote: Do not include conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident’s current status, or do not drive the resident’s plan of care during the 7-day look-back period, as these would be considered inactive diagnoses.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check off each active disease; check all that apply.

source.quote: Check off each active disease. Check all that apply.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If none of the listed diagnoses (including pneumonia) are active within the past 7 days, code I7900, None of the above active diagnoses.

source.quote: I7900, none of the above active diagnoses within the past 7 days

federal_coding_rules.rule: Specific physician documentation that the condition is active is sufficient to code it active and requires no additional confirmation.

source.quote: The physician may specifically indicate that a condition is active. Specific documentation may be found in progress notes, most recent history and physical, transfer notes, hospital discharge summary, etc.

federal_coding_rules.rule: In the absence of specific documentation that the disease is active, recent onset or acute exacerbation indicated by a positive study, test or procedure, hospitalization for acute symptoms, and/or recent change in therapy in the last 7 days may confirm active disease (e.g., new diagnosis of pneumonia indicated by chest X-ray).

source.quote: Recent onset or acute exacerbation of the disease or condition indicated by a positive study, test or procedure, hospitalization for acute symptoms and/or recent change in therapy in the last 7 days. Examples of a recent onset or acute exacerbation include the following: new diagnosis of pneumonia indicated by chest X-ray

federal_coding_rules.rule: Symptoms and abnormal signs indicating ongoing or decompensated disease in the last 7 days may confirm active disease, but a symptom must be specifically attributed to the disease by a physician (e.g., a productive cough would confirm a diagnosis of pneumonia if specifically noted as such by a physician).

source.quote: For example, a productive cough would confirm a diagnosis of pneumonia if specifically noted as such by a physician.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Listing the diagnosis on the resident's medical record problem list is not sufficient for determining active or inactive status.

source.quote: Listing a disease/diagnosis (e.g., arthritis) on the resident’s medical record problem list is not sufficient for determining active or inactive status.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Ongoing therapy with medications or other interventions in the last 7 days to manage the condition, requiring monitoring for therapeutic efficacy or for potentially severe side effects, indicates active disease.

source.quote: Ongoing therapy with medications or other interventions to manage a condition that requires monitoring for therapeutic efficacy or to monitor potentially severe side effects in the last 7 days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Routine nursing monitoring of medications for adverse effects does not by itself establish active disease; for coding purposes that monitoring relates to management of pharmacotherapy, not management or monitoring of the underlying disease.

source.quote: It is expected that nurses monitor all medications for adverse effects as part of usual nursing practice. For coding purposes, this monitoring relates to management of pharmacotherapy and not to management or monitoring of the underlying disease.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a disease or condition is not specifically listed among the checkbox items, enter the diagnosis and ICD code in item I8000, Additional active diagnosis.

source.quote: If a disease or condition is not specifically listed, enter the diagnosis and ICD code in item I8000, Additional active diagnosis.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the resident is receiving aftercare following hospitalization, a Z code may be assigned; when Z codes are used, another diagnosis for the related primary medical condition should be checked in items I0100–I7900 or entered in I8000.

source.quote: When Z codes are used, another diagnosis for the related primary medical condition should be checked in items I0100–I7900 or entered in I8000.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If pneumonia is the primary medical condition coded in I0020B, it must also be included in items I0100–I8000, Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days.

source.quote: Include the primary medical condition coded in item I0020B in items I0100–I8000: Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days.

federal.criterion: Physician-documented diagnosis of pneumonia (or by NP, PA, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) within the last 60 days, found in the medical record.

source.quote: The disease conditions in this section require a physician-documented diagnosis (or by a nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) in the last 60 days.

federal.notes: Step 1 of the two-step assessment process.

federal.criterion: Acceptable medical record sources for the physician diagnosis: progress notes, the most recent history and physical, transfer documents, discharge summaries, diagnosis/problem list, and other resources as available; if a diagnosis/problem list is used, only diagnoses confirmed by the physician should be entered.

source.quote: Medical record sources for physician diagnoses include progress notes, the most recent history and physical, transfer documents, discharge summaries, diagnosis/ problem list, and other resources as available. If a diagnosis/problem list is used, only diagnoses confirmed by the physician should be entered.

federal.criterion: Diagnoses communicated verbally must be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure follow-up.

source.quote: it is also essential that diagnoses communicated verbally be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure follow-up.

federal.criterion: Diagnostic information, including past history obtained from family members and close contacts, must be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure validity and follow-up.

source.quote: Diagnostic information, including past history obtained from family members and close contacts, must also be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure validity and follow-up.

federal.criterion: Evidence in the last 7 days from these medical record sources supporting active status: transfer documents, physician progress notes, recent history and physical, recent discharge summaries, nursing assessments, nursing care plans, medication sheets, doctor's orders, consults and official diagnostic reports.

source.quote: Check the following information sources in the medical record for the last 7 days to identify “active” diagnoses: transfer documents, physician progress notes, recent history and physical, recent discharge summaries, nursing assessments, nursing care plans, medication sheets, doctor’s orders, consults and official diagnostic reports, and other sources as available.

federal.criterion: Radiological report (e.g., chest X-ray) documenting new onset of pneumonia may be used as a source to confirm active disease in the absence of specific documentation of activity.

source.quote: new diagnosis of pneumonia indicated by chest X-ray; hospitalization for fractured hip; or a blood transfusion for a hematocrit of 24. Sources may include radiological reports, hospital discharge summaries, doctor’s orders, etc.

federal.notes: Framed as an indicator that may be used, not as required documentation.

federal.criterion: Physician notation specifically attributing a symptom (e.g., productive cough) to pneumonia, in radiological reports, nursing assessments and care plans, or progress notes.

source.quote: Sometimes signs and symptoms can be nonspecific and could be caused by several disease processes. Therefore, a symptom must be specifically attributed to the disease.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section I pages do not tie item I2000 to a payment or case-mix classification. (Item I0020 references the Medicare Part A stay, but that is a separate item and does not state a case-mix use for I2000.)

conflicts.topic: Coexisting look-back windows for Section I active diagnoses (60-day identification vs. 7-day active status)

positions.claim: Diagnosis identification (Step 1) uses a 60-day look-back period.

source.quote: Diagnosis identification (Step 1) is a 60-day look-back period.

positions.claim: Diagnosis status (active or inactive, Step 2) uses a 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Diagnosis status: Active or Inactive (Step 2) is a 7-day look-back period (except for Item I2300 UTI, which does not use the active 7-day look-back period).

conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the document itself: the two windows are complementary steps, not competing rules — the diagnosis must be documented within 60 days and must be active during the 7-day look-back period (p. I-9). lookback_days is recorded as the 7-day observation window for active status.
